newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japn, Thailand not discussing Thai finance woes-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japn, Thailand not discussing Thai finance woes-MOF.

text.p: Japanese and Thai authorities are not in detailed discussions on how to help Thailand deal with its financial problems, including its weak currency, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.
"We are exchanging opinions and information about Thailand with Thai and other related parties," he said.

"However, there have been absolutely no discussions on a detailed scheme on the issue," Ogawa said, after he was asked how Japan was going to help Thailand deal with its financial woes following the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht last week.
He said the ministry was currently coordinating schedules with Thai authorities for a meeting between Thai and Japanese finance ministers planned in Tokyo next week.

Japanese banking sources said Thailand's Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya will explain to Japanese bankers the recent situation surrounding the Thai currency during his visit here next week. Thanong and Thai Foreign Affairs Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn will meet representatives from Japanese commercial banks on July 17, the sources said. The two ministers will be
in Tokyo on July 17 and 18 for an unofficial visit.

Thailand plans to raise a total of $10 billion, consisting of $5 billion in loans from banks and $5 billion in bond issues, in order to replenish reserves that were severely depleted when it defended its currency against speculative

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily said on Thursday that Japan's government and financial sector would take a leadership role in extending financial aid to Thailand, working alongside international organisations and other countries. (c) Reuters Limited 1997
